significance: A Tulja Bhavani temple built in the mid-1950s by Kethavath Chandru Naik with local support, standing above the Krishna river near Nagarjuna Sagar Dam on the edge of the Nallamala forest.
story: The goddess is said to have come to the aid of Anubuti, a sage's wife whose penance on the Mandakini was being disturbed by the demon Kukur, and to have taken the name Tulja Bhavani after destroying him.
